### Observed differences

- Participation shifted only slightly and in both directions: A01, A03, A04 and A05 each appeared in about 45 in 100 traces in the earlier window and about 49 in 100 in the later window, while A02, A06, A07 and A08 each fell from about 55 to 51 in 100; the other flagged activities moved by roughly 2–4 in 100 traces in either direction (for example A32–A34 rose from about 49 to 52 in 100, while A28, A30 and A31 fell from about 51 to 49 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024]
- A10 and A11 occurred in every trace in both windows, but their repetitions became somewhat less frequent: about 1.7 occurrences per trace with repeats in about 40 in 100 traces earlier, versus about 1.55 occurrences per trace with repeats in about 33 in 100 traces later. [OCC009, OCC010]
- A39 was observed more often in the later window (about 58 in 100 traces earlier versus 65 in 100 later; about 0.79 versus 0.90 occurrences per trace), while A40 and A41 were observed less often (about 66 in 100 traces earlier versus 62 in 100 later; about 0.96 versus 0.86 occurrences per trace). [OCC028, OCC029, OCC030]
- Successor shares moved by a few percentage points in several places: after A01 the share leading to A03 rose from about 34% to 45% while the share to A04 fell from about 36% to 27%; after A02 the share to A06 rose from about 27% to 38%; after A07 the share to A08 rose from about 23% to 33%; after A38 the share to A39 rose from about 45% to 51% while the share to A40 fell from about 55% to 49%; and after A39 the share returning to A38 rose from about 36% to 42%. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR007, DIR027, DIR028]
- Many other differences sit at noise level: the routing splits after A20, A24, A27 and A29 changed by only about one to two percentage points, and most flagged items show empirical strengths between about 0.01 and 0.55, meaning random re-splits of the same traces regularly produce differences of this size; only about 13 of the 59 items exceed 0.6. [DIR008, DIR013, DIR014, DIR015, DIR017, DIR019, OCC001, OCC011, OCC013, OCC027]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The differences are small (mostly a few percentage points), scattered across nearly every activity in both directions, and even the strongest items are of a size that random re-splits of an unchanged process regularly exceed, so ordinary sampling variability between the two 200-trace windows cannot be ruled out [OCC001, OCC009, DIR014, DIR027].
